summary.short: City rules (6 RCNY Subchapter T) under which employers and employment agencies using automated employment decision tools must obtain a bias audit within one year before use, publish audit results and the distribution date, and give candidates and employees notice before use.
summary.long: Subchapter T of Title 6 of the Rules of the City of New York implements Local Law 144 of 2021 on automated employment decision tools (AEDTs). It covers employers and employment agencies that use an AEDT to screen candidates or employees considered for promotion in New York City. An AEDT may not be used or continued in use if more than one year has passed since its most recent bias audit (§ 5-301(a)). The bias audit, conducted by an independent auditor, must calculate selection rates, or scoring rates for scoring tools, and impact ratios for sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories, and report individuals in unknown categories. An auditor may exclude categories under 2% of the data, with justification (§ 5-301(b)-(d)). Audits must use historical data, with test data allowed only where historical data is insufficient (§ 5-302). Before use, employers must publish the audit date, a results summary and the distribution date on their website, and keep them posted for at least six months after last use (§ 5-303). Notice must go to city residents at least 10 business days before use, with instructions for requesting an alternative process or accommodation where available, though no alternative process is required (§ 5-304(a)-(c)). Employers must also publish data retention and data source information and answer written requests within 30 days (§ 5-304(d)). The excerpt contains no penalty provisions and gives no effective date.

notes: Excerpt: the text is the Notice of Adoption and Section 1 (new Subchapter T, Sections 5-300 to 5-304) only, so Administrative Code Sections 20-870 and 20-871, Local Law 144 of 2021 and the EEOC materials are referenced but not reproduced. Internal inconsistencies: (1) the notice says brackets mark deleted material, yet bracketed words such as [Not Hispanic or Latino] appear inside operative examples in Sections 5-301(b)(3)(ii) and 5-301(c)(4)(ii); (2) Section 5-301(b)(3)(i) reads 'Sex categories (e.g., ...)' while Section 5-301(c)(4)(i) reads 'Sex categories (i.e., ...)'; (3) Section 5-301(c)(4)(i) concerns scoring rates but its example speaks of selection. The notice says new material is underlined; the plain-text copy does not show underlining, so new versus restated text cannot be checked. No named firms appear; employers, employment agencies and independent auditors are generic addressees. section_status entries are marked not_applicable only because the schema requires a status; the relations and entities sections are populated above.

evidence.quote: “Automated employment decision tool” or “AEDT” means “Automated employment decision tool” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code where the phrase “to substantially assist or replace discretionary decision making” means:

definitions.defined_in: § 5-300 (by reference to § 20-870 of the Administrative Code)

evidence.quote: “Bias audit” means “Bias audit” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code.

“Candidate for employment” means a person who has applied for a specific employment position by submitting the necessary information or items in the format required by the employer or employment agency.
“Category” means any component 1 category required to be reported by employers pursuant to subsection (c) of section 2000e-8 of title 42 of the United States Code
“Distribution date” means the date the employer or employment agency began using a specific AEDT.

definitions.defined_in: § 5-300 (by reference to § 20-870 of the Administrative Code)

evidence.quote: “Employment decision” means “Employment decision” as defined by § 20-870 of the Code.
“Employment agency” means “Employment agency” as defined by 6 RCNY § 5249.
“Historical data” means data collected during an employer or employment agency’s use of an AEDT to assess candidates for employment or employees for promotion.
“Independent auditor” means a person or group that is capable of exercising objective and impartial judgment on all issues within the scope of a bias audit of an AEDT.

“Impact ratio” means either (1) the selection rate for a category divided by the selection rate of the most selected category or (2) the scoring rate for a category divided by the scoring rate for the highest scoring category.

“Scoring Rate” means the rate at which individuals in a category receive a score above the sample’s median score, where the score has been calculated by an AEDT.
“Screen” means to make a determination about whether a candidate for employment or employee being considered for promotion should be selected or advanced in the hiring or promotion process.
“Selection rate” means the rate at which individuals in a category are either selected to move forward in the hiring process or assigned a classification by an AEDT.

obligations.summary: Employers and employment agencies may not use or continue to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since its most recent bias audit (applies to employment agencies as well as employers).
obligations.conditional_on: More than one year has passed since the most recent bias audit of the AEDT.

evidence.quote: An employer or employment agency may not use or continue to use an AEDT if more than one year has passed since the most recent bias audit of the AEDT.

obligations.summary: A bias audit of an AEDT must, at a minimum, calculate selection rates or scoring rates and impact ratios for each category, separately for sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories, for each group where the AEDT classifies candidates, and indicate the number of individuals in unknown categories; an independent auditor may exclude categories under 2% of the data, with justification stated in the summary of results.
obligations.conditional_on: The AEDT selects, classifies or scores candidates for employment or employees being considered for promotion.

evidence.quote: a bias audit must, at a minimum:

obligations.summary: A bias audit conducted under section 5-301 must use historical data of the AEDT, which may come from one or more employers or employment agencies; an individual employer may rely on another employer's historical data only if it provided its own historical data to the auditor or has never used the AEDT.

evidence.quote: A bias audit conducted pursuant to section 5-301 of this Chapter must use historical data of the AEDT.

obligations.summary: An employer or employment agency may rely on a bias audit using test data if insufficient historical data is available for a statistically significant audit; the summary of results must then explain why historical data was not used and how the test data was generated and obtained.
obligations.conditional_on: Insufficient historical data is available to conduct a statistically significant bias audit.

evidence.quote: an employer or employment agency may rely on a bias audit that uses test data if insufficient historical data is available

obligations.summary: Before using an AEDT, an employer or employment agency in the city must publish on the employment section of its website, clearly and conspicuously (or via a clearly identified hyperlink), the date of the most recent bias audit with a summary of results (data source, unknown-category count, applicant numbers, selection or scoring rates and impact ratios) and the AEDT distribution date.
obligations.applies_from: Before the use of an AEDT
obligations.conditional_on: The employer or employment agency is in the city and uses an AEDT.

evidence.quote: Before the use of an AEDT, an employer or employment agency in the city must make the following publicly available on the employment section of their website in a clear and conspicuous manner

obligations.summary: The employer or employment agency must keep the summary of results and distribution date posted for at least 6 months after its latest use of the AEDT for an employment decision.
obligations.applies_from: At least 6 months after its latest use of the AEDT for an employment decision
obligations.conditional_on: The AEDT is used for an employment decision.

evidence.quote: An employer or employment agency must keep the summary of results and distribution date posted for at least 6 months after its latest use of the AEDT for an employment decision.

obligations.summary: Notice under Code § 20-871(b)(1) and (2) to city candidates for employment and employees considered for promotion must include instructions for requesting an alternative selection process or reasonable accommodation where available, and must be given at least 10 business days before AEDT use (via website, job posting, written policy, or mail or e-mail); no alternative selection process is required.
obligations.applies_from: At least 10 business days before use of an AEDT
obligations.conditional_on: The AEDT is used to assess candidates for employment or employees being considered for promotion who reside in the city.

evidence.quote: The notice required by § 20-871(b)(1) of the Code must include instructions for how an individual can request an alternative selection process or a reasonable accommodation under other laws, if available.

obligations.summary: The employer or employment agency must provide information on its website, clearly and conspicuously, about its AEDT data retention policy, the type of data collected and the source of the data, as required under Code § 20-871(b)(3).
obligations.conditional_on: The AEDT is used to assess candidates for employment or employees considered for promotion.

evidence.quote: Provide information on the employment section of its website in a clear and conspicuous manner about its AEDT data retention policy

obligations.summary: The employer or employment agency must post instructions on its website for making a written request for information about the AEDT, provide the requested information within 30 days of receiving a written request, and where disclosure would violate law or interfere with a law enforcement investigation, explain to the candidate or employee why it cannot disclose.
obligations.conditional_on: A written request is received from a candidate for employment or an employee considered for promotion.

evidence.quote: if a written request is received, provide such information within 30 days

enforcement.note: This text contains no sanction, fine, penalty, revocation, suspension or blocking provision. It sets out bias audit, published-results and notice requirements under § 5-300 to § 5-304 and refers to Administrative Code § 20-870 and § 20-871 for the underlying duties, but does not state any penalty or enforcement regime. Any penalty provisions would lie outside this text and are not annotated.
